## Employee
- Name: Sagnibha Roy (no id)
- Role: Maintenance Planner, Maintenance
- Plant / unit: Raiganj  / Unit 100

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Unit 100 maintenance prioritization – unwritten rules and backstage trade-offs
topics.rationale: CMMS work orders show schedules, but not how you decide what gets done first when resources are tight, or which tasks you quietly defer without raising flags.
seed_questions: When the schedule is overloaded, how do you really decide which jobs slip and which get expedited?
Can you walk me through a recent example where the formal priority didn't match what you actually did?

topics.title: Half-finished maintenance improvement projects in Unit 100
topics.rationale: Projects like RCM implementation or PdM expansion may have stalled for reasons nobody wrote down – scope creep, vendor dropout, internal resistance.
seed_questions: Which maintenance improvement project in Unit 100 did you start but never finish, and what stopped it?
If someone tried to resurrect that project tomorrow, what landmines should they watch for?

topics.title: Unit 100 critical rotating equipment – undocumented failure patterns and workarounds
topics.rationale: Pumps and compressors often have repeat failures that are patched rather than root-solved; the true failure history lives in your memory, not in the logbooks.
seed_questions: Which piece of rotating equipment in Unit 100 gives you the most sleepless nights, and what failure signs do you look for that aren't in the PM checklist?
Can you describe a recurring failure where the documented fix never lasted, and what actual workaround you use?

topics.title: Unit 100 shutdown planning – unwritten coordination tricks
topics.rationale: Official shutdown procedures rarely capture how you negotiate overlapping permits, manage hungry contractors, or handle last-minute production pushbacks.
seed_questions: What's your secret to getting production to release equipment on time during a turnaround?
Can you give an example of a shutdown where you deviated from the plan because of an on-the-spot call, and what was the outcome?

topics.title: The informal expert network for Unit 100 equipment
topics.rationale: You know which millwright understands the vibration on that finicky blower, and which operator can sweet-talk the DCS into submission – none of this is in the contact list.
seed_questions: If a critical pump acts up at 2 a.m. and the on-call tech is stuck, who would you personally call and why?
Are there any retired or transferred people whose memory you still tap into for Unit 100 issues?

topics.title: Successor advice – open risks and hidden maintenance debt in Unit 100
topics.rationale: A formal handover document exists, but you know what will keep you up at night after you leave: overdue overhauls, bypassed safety switches, or stretched PM intervals.
seed_questions: What is the single biggest risk you wish the incoming planner knew about on Day 1?
If you had one week to prepare your replacement, which three things would you walk them through that are nowhere in the files?

topics.title: Unit 100 spare parts inventory – unwritten stocking logic
topics.rationale: The ERP shows min/max levels, but not why you override them for certain seals or why you hoard obsolete couplings from a defunct supplier.
seed_questions: Which spare parts for Unit 100 do you keep extra stock of, against the system's recommendations, and why?
Are there items where the official lead time is dangerously wrong, and how do you compensate?

topics.title: Vendor and supplier quirks specific to Unit 100 equipment
topics.rationale: Vendor documentation is polished; your knowledge of which local supplier actually meets specs, or that a certain OEM tech is the only one who can calibrate that instrument, is not.
seed_questions: Are there any equipment vendors or service providers for Unit 100 where you bypass the official channel and call a specific person directly?
Which supplier has repeatedly let you down in subtle ways that never appear in the formal vendor scorecards?

topics.title: Unit 100 predictive maintenance – early-warning signs only you recognise
topics.rationale: Condition monitoring data is captured, but you combine it with sounds, smells, and operator chatter to call a failure weeks before the trend alarm triggers.
seed_questions: What's the most unusual early warning sign you've learned to trust that isn't in any PdM manual?
Can you describe a time you overrode a vibration alarm because you 'knew' the machine was still healthy – and were right?

topics.title: Root cause ghosts – Unit 100 failures that were never truly solved
topics.rationale: Some incidents are closed with 'procedure not followed' when you know deeper design or fatigue issues are at play; the real story is in your head.
seed_questions: Which repetitive failure in Unit 100 do you believe has a different root cause than what the final report stated?
Have you ever found a workaround that fixed a problem for years, even though the root cause was never officially addressed?

topics.title: Maintenance plan templates – Unit 100 customizations that are not in the SOP
topics.rationale: The official PM plan is generic; you have likely tweaked frequencies, task lists, or added informal inspections based on observed wear rates or seasonal patterns.
seed_questions: Which PM tasks in Unit 100 do you think are done too often or not often enough, and how did you adjust them unofficially?
Are there any seasonal maintenance preparations you always schedule even though the written plan doesn't mention them?

topics.title: CMMS data reality – gaps and workarounds in the Unit 100 job history
topics.rationale: What you enter in the CMMS is often a summary; the actual failure description, parts used, and time spent may differ significantly but remain unwritten.
seed_questions: What never gets recorded accurately in the CMMS for Unit 100 jobs, and how do you retain that info?
If you needed to find the real repair history for a specific asset, what informal notes or people would you rely on instead of the system?

topics.title: Maintenance safety near-misses and unwritten red flags in Unit 100
topics.rationale: Official safety reports capture incidents, but you know which equipment combinations or transient conditions worry you, even if no near-miss was officially logged.
seed_questions: Which task in Unit 100 makes you hold your breath every time, even though it's considered routine on paper?
Can you think of a time you stopped a job because of a gut feeling, and what tipped you off?

topics.title: Budget and cost-control shortcuts that keep Unit 100 maintenance afloat
topics.rationale: Capital vs. expense decisions, or creative ways you reclassify work orders to stretch the budget, are rarely written down but are essential for the next planner.
seed_questions: How do you actually manage the maintenance budget when costs start running over – what lines do you move or delay?
Are there any informal 'understandings' with contractors about billing or scope that help keep costs in control?

topics.title: Legacy equipment and obsolete technology – Unit 100's hidden Achilles' heels
topics.rationale: As the plant ages, you know which controllers, valves, or motors are one failure away from a long outage because spares are unavailable or expertise has vanished.
seed_questions: Which piece of Unit 100 equipment are you most worried about because it can't be replaced easily anymore?
What's the ugliest improvisation you've had to maintain to keep something running, and what would the next person need to know if it fails?
